## On the out-of-sequence DR finding: correct from the diff, wrong in fact

The architect panel asks me to renumber DR-094 to DR-092, on the grounds that DR-091 is the highest record on disk and CLAUDE.md's Decision Register rule says "next number = max(existing DR-NNN in docs/decisions/) + 1".

That is exactly what the files show, and it is the wrong action. DR-092 and DR-093 are both claimed by open pull requests:

| id | claimed by |
|---|---|
| DR-092 | #1835 (open) - harness refresh silently reverts a repo |
| DR-093 | #1866 (open) |
| DR-094 | this PR |

I did not pick 094 by hand. The repo's own `dr-id-collision` gate rejected 092 and named the replacement:

```
DR id collision - 1 id is already taken:
  - DR-092 is already claimed by PR #1835 (docs/decisions/DR-092.md)

Next free id: DR-094 - the max across main AND every open PR, plus one.
```

and after the renumber:

```
DR id check: DR-094 is free on main and across every open PR. (Next free id: DR-095.)
exit code: 0
```

**Why the reviewer could not have known.** The panel runs as a no-tools agent reading the diff as untrusted data, with no network. Open PRs are invisible to it by construction, so "the highest record on disk is DR-091" is the only evidence available and the conclusion follows from it. This is the same asymmetry the reviewers hit elsewhere: they cannot verify anything that is not in the diff, so they must defer on it. Not holding it against the panel; recording why the instruction is not being followed.

**Renumbering to 092 would cause the harm the gate exists to prevent.** If #1835 merges first, two records share one id, one of them becomes uncitable, and a merge can silently overwrite an already-accepted decision (#1226).

Keeping DR-094. Filed the underlying rule conflict separately rather than arguing it here.

## This PR cannot clear ai-review while it carries DR-094, and that is structural rather than a fixable defect

Recording the loop so the next reader (or the next re-review) does not spend another round on it.

The architect panel raises a blocking finding instructing me to renumber DR-094 to DR-092, citing CLAUDE.md's rule that the next number is `max(existing DR-NNN in docs/decisions/) + 1`. On disk, DR-091 is the highest, so that instruction follows correctly from the only evidence the panel has.

**It will recur on every re-review.** The panel is a no-tools agent reading the diff with no network, so open pull requests are invisible to it by construction. As long as this PR carries an id above the on-disk maximum, the same finding is produced, and the label cannot go green.

Meanwhile the repo's enforced gate refuses the renumber:

```
$ npx tsx scripts/check-dr-id-collision.ts --repo AIClarityAU/minspec --pr 1956 --base main
DR id collision - 1 id is already taken:
  - DR-092 is already claimed by PR #1835 (docs/decisions/DR-092.md)
Next free id: DR-094 - the max across main AND every open PR, plus one.
```

Re-measured just now: DR-092 and DR-093 are still absent from `origin/main`, so #1835 and #1866 are still open and still hold them.

So the two instructions are in direct conflict, one of them is enforced and one is prose, and following the prose one would cause the silent overwrite the gate exists to prevent (#1226).

## Three ways out, and which actually works

1. **Wait for #1835 and #1866 to merge.** DR-094 then becomes in-sequence on disk and the finding evaporates. Costs nothing but is entirely outside this PR's control.
2. **Renumber to DR-092.** Rejected - it causes the collision.
3. **Fix the rule the panel is quoting (#1979).** If CLAUDE.md said "run `check-dr-id-collision.ts`; it reports the next free id across main and every open PR", there would be no formula to cite and the finding would not be generated.

Option 3 is the only one that both unblocks this PR and stops it recurring for every future concurrent DR. **#1979 is therefore not a backlog nit - it is this PR's blocker**, and I have re-scoped it accordingly rather than leaving it filed as a convention tidy-up.

## Unchanged

The other blocking finding stands and is correct: DR-094 is `status: proposed`, and relaxing AC-3 rests on it. Acceptance is a human act under DR-029. That one is not a deadlock, it is simply waiting on the founder.

Branch updated to `origin/main` this turn; suite 6113 passed, lint 0 errors.

commits.messageBody:
Root cause of the blocker found while wiring: MAX_TTL_SECONDS was 600 and
clampExpiry REFUSES anything above it, but GitHub installation tokens are fixed
at one hour. `POST /app/installations/{id}/access_tokens` accepts only
`repositories`, `repository_ids` and `permissions`; there is no lifetime field,
and the docs state the tokens "expire one hour from the time you create them".
So the broker would have rejected 100% of real mints and the live path could
only ever answer "auth returned an unusable expiry". A ceiling below the
platform's floor is not a strict gate, it is an off switch.

FR-3 already said the honest thing ("target <=10 min; GitHub's ceiling is 1h").
AC-3 hardened that target into a limit and the code implemented the limit. The
gate that should have caught it could not exist: no test could mint a real
token, and the one test covering this asserted REFUSAL of a 60-minute token,
which encoded the bug as the expected behaviour.

Changes:

- `index.ts` runs route, method, audience, bearer, OIDC verify, body shape,
  claim match, then mint - in that order, with the single credential-bearing
  return last. Verification precedes body parsing so an unauthorised caller
  never makes the broker deserialise input.
- `app-auth.ts`: the real InstallationTokenFactory, and the only place the App
  private key is used. Resolves the installation via an App JWT, then mints
  scoped to one repo. `repositoryNames` takes bare names, not `owner/repo`.
- `createFetchHandler(deps)` injects the JWKS lookup and the factory, mirroring
  why `mint.ts` takes its factory as an argument: otherwise every test past
  verification needs GitHub's live JWKS, and a test that needs the network does
  not run in CI.
- `MAX_TTL_SECONDS` 600 -> 3600, keeping the refusal for anything beyond what
  the platform documents.
- `BROKER_AUDIENCE` declared in wrangler.toml, with a guard: an absent audience
  500s everything, and a MISMATCH between broker and workflow 401s everything
  while reading as a signature problem.
- Error codes: added `unexpected_field`, `unsupported_profile` (already emitted
  by `decide()` and pinned by its tests, while design.md had no 400 member at
  all) and `broker_misconfigured` (our deployment, not the caller's request).
  design.md's contract updated rather than the deviation left unstated.

Spec corrections, all recorded in place with reasoning: AC-3's unachievable TTL,
three further <=10 min claims in design.md including the sequence diagram, and
task 1.3's restatement.

Task 1.4 split. 1.4a (this) is verified: 21 new assertions across a
step-by-step refusal matrix with a happy-path control, real RS256 signatures and
no network, plus `wrangler deploy --dry-run` proving it bundles for the Workers
runtime at 30.05 KiB gzip with no `nodejs_compat`. 1.4b (workflow + e2e) is
blocked twice over and NOT started: no broker is deployed, and this repo holds
the App secrets so `ai-review.yml` always takes slice 4's override path - the
broker branch would never execute here, so AC-7 needs the dogfood repo.

`broker-scaffold.test.ts` converted rather than deleted: its 501 assertions
became "an unconfigured broker refuses everything", so every no-credential
assertion survives unchanged.

Full suite 6057 passed, 3 expected fail. Lint 0 errors.

factory, which is right for testing the decision path but meant
`makeInstallationTokenFactory` - the only code that touches the App private key -
was never invoked by any test. Its guards are all synchronous or fetch-shaped and

- `broker-app-auth.test.ts` covers the credential-presence branches (including

  four malformed-repository forms, the lookup-failure path and the missing-id

Also from the review, and one that mattered more than its severity:

- MAX_TTL_SECONDS sat at exactly 3600, GitHub's own figure. GitHub stamps
  `expires_at` on GitHub's clock and the Worker compares against Cloudflare's, so
  whenever the Worker's clock is behind by more than the mint round-trip,
  `expiresAt - now` exceeds the bound and a legitimate token is refused. That
  re-creates the off switch this PR was written to remove - intermittently and
  only under drift, which is strictly worse because it would be unreproducible.
  Added CLOCK_SKEW_GRACE_SECONDS = 300 above the ceiling. Mutation-tested in both
  directions: removing the grace reddens the skew test, and inflating it to two
  hours reddens the three tests that keep the guard's teeth.

  claimed "a TTL of ten minutes or less" 42 lines above the constant this PR set
  to 3600, and also claimed to be "the only place the App private key is used"
  when the key edge had moved to `app-auth.ts`. Two more copies of the ten-minute
  figure in `index.ts` and `broker-scaffold.test.ts`. I had grepped the specs for
  `≤10 min` and never grepped source for the spelled-out form.

- The `broker_misconfigured` 500 preceded the bearer check, so an
  unauthenticated caller could distinguish a configured broker from an
  unconfigured one. Bearer check now comes first: nothing is answered before
  authentication. The scaffold test's expectations follow the new ordering rather
  than being relaxed.

- `owner`/`repo` path segments are encoded, so the property does not depend on
  the values arriving from a GitHub-signed claim.

- DR-092 records the accepted residual risk the architect asked for: a
  broker-minted token is usable for up to an hour after the run that requested
  it, that cannot be reduced by configuration, and it is accepted because the
  alternative is not a shorter token but every adopter holding the App key.
  Rejected alternatives recorded per DR-086 §4, including run-end revocation,
  which is the option most likely to be right later.

- tasks.md no longer presents the bundle size as checked-in evidence, and names
